item.research_question: How does varying Ti content (x = 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7) affect the microstructure, microhardness, and corrosion resistance of CoCrFeNiTix high entropy alloy coatings prepared by laser cladding?
item.material_system: CoCrFeNiTix (x = 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7) high entropy alloy coatings on Q235 steel substrate
item.processing_route: Laser cladding using a high power semiconductor laser (LDF3000-60) with laser power of 1.3 kW, scan speed of 4.5 mm/s, overlap rate of 30%, spot diameter of 2 mm, and argon protective gas at 9 L/min carrier gas speed
item.test_conditions: Electrochemical testing in 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution at room temperature using a three-electrode configuration with voltage swept from -1.5 V to 1.5 V at 1 mV/s; microhardness measured under 500 g load for 10 s
key_findings: CoCrFeNiTi0.1 adopts a face-centered cubic (FCC) phase, while CoCrFeNiTi0.3 exhibits an FCC phase and a tetragonal FeCr phase.
CoCrFeNiTi0.5 adopts an FCC phase, a tetragonal FeCr phase, and a rhombohedral NiTi phase.
CoCrFeNiTi0.7 contains an FCC phase, a tetragonal FeCr phase, a rhombohedral NiTi phase, and a hexagonal CoTi phase.
Peak microhardness increases from 310 Hv to 830 Hv as Ti content increases from x=0.1 to x=0.7.
Ni and Ti are enriched in the interdendritic regions, whereas Cr and Fe are enriched in the dendrites.
Pitting corrosion is the main form of corrosion, with small dish-shaped pits of 1–5 µm diameter observed.
Corrosion current densities are much lower than other HEAs, and corrosion resistance improves as Ti content increases.
The passivation film is mainly composed of TiO2 and Cr2O3, with higher relative atomic percentages of Cr and Ti on the surface than in the bulk.
item.mechanism: The improved corrosion resistance is attributed to a dense passivation film composed of TiO2 and Cr2O3, which creates high energy barriers for Cl- ion adsorption and diffusion at the Cr2O3/TiO2 interfaces, thereby resisting pitting. Increased hardness is due to lattice distortion from Ti addition, reduced secondary dendritic arm spacing, and dispersion strengthening from hard precipitates.
item.limitations: The mechanisms of pitting corrosion have not been completely elucidated due to the limitations of the available detection methods.
quotes: The results show that CoCrFeNiTi0.1 adopts a face-centered cubic (FCC) phase, CoCrFeNiTi0.3 exhibits an FCC phase and a tetragonal FeCr phase.
The energy barriers at the Cr2O3/TiO2 interfaces are higher than the ones at the Cr2O3/Nb2O5 interfaces.

Question: How does varying Ti content (x = 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7) affect the microstructure, microhardness, and corrosion resistance of CoCrFeNiTix high entropy alloy coatings prepared by laser cladding?. Test conditions: Electrochemical testing in 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution at room temperature using a three-electrode configuration with voltage swept from -1.5 V to 1.5 V at 1 mV/s; microhardness measured under 500 g load for 10 s. Increased hardness is due to lattice distortion from Ti addition, reduced secondary dendritic arm spacing, and dispersion strengthening from hard precipitates.. Limitations: The mechanisms of pitting corrosion have not been completely elucidated due to the limitations of the available detection methods..
